newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait police clash with gunmen on Iraq border.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait police clash with gunmen on Iraq border.

text.p: Kuwait said on Tuesday gunmen on the Iraqi side of its border have clashed with its border police after they opened fire at a Kuwaiti observation post.
"The shooting took place at dawn on Sunday," Colonel Badr Saleh of the interior ministry told Reuters by telephone. "They were about four gunmen and a driver," he added.
"They opened fire at a border observation post and the Kuwaiti police had to return fire," he said, adding that the shooting lasted for about 30 minutes at al-Abdali border area.
Saleh said the ministry informed the United Nations Iraq-Kuwait Observation Mission (UNIKOM) of the incident.
"So far we cannot confirm anything about the (reported) incident," UNIKOM's military public affairs officer, Captain Massimo Amadei, said. "We are still investigating."
Kuwait's al-Watan newspaper said "the Iraqi group consisted of about five people who carried machineguns".
UNIKOM monitors a demilitarised strip straddling the border of the two countries since the 1991 Gulf War that ended Iraq's seven-month occupation of the oil-rich Gulf state.
Saleh said there were no injuries on the Kuwait side. He said he was not aware of any injuries on the Iraqi side.
Kuwait's media have often reported raids on border farms in the zone by gunmen stealing money, vehicles and equipment.
Iraq-Kuwait border posts have been closed for normal traffic since the War, but Iraqis have regularly came accross to smuggle goods or seek asylum in third countries, diplomats say.
